brief_summary: A rising curve plotting perceived smoothness against actuation count, climbing steeply from 0 to roughly 300 actuations before flattening into a near-plateau through 1000+. A dashed vertical marker flags the plateau point, with annotations for burr wear plus lube spread driving the steep early section and spring settling as a smaller, slightly later contribution.
data_sources: switch-break-in-myth.mdx § 'Where the returns stop' — 'Most of the lube redistribution and most of the burr-wearing happens in the first handful of hundreds of actuations ... A switch run for a thousand cycles on a bulk tester and a switch run for three thousand will feel close to identical.'

switch-break-in-myth.mdx § 'What's actually moving in there' — 'Springs take a first set ... This is adjacent to break-in rather than break-in itself, and it's a smaller, faster effect than the other two'
